reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that non-leader figures (the Israelite people) possess and exercise agency. They quarrel with Moses (וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה), actively demand water (תְּנוּ־ לָנוּ מַיִם), lodge complaints against Moses (וַיָּלֶן הָעָם עַל־ מֹשֶׁה), voice grievances about their circumstances, and explicitly test God (נַסֹּתָֽם אֶת־ יְהוָה). These are not passive behaviors but deliberate acts of will and choice. While leadership (Moses and God) carries greater authority and directs the ultimate resolution, the common people are clearly portrayed as active agents making demands, registering protest, and testing divine commitment—not as passive subjects lacking agency.
